title: Djokovic makes a Beijing comeback as Sabalenka discusses self-pressure
summary:
Novak Djokovic protected his unbeaten record in Beijing with a demanding comeback at the China Open. The six-time champion defeated China's Bu Yunchaokete 4-6 7-6 (7-2) 6-2 to advance to the third round.

Bu took the opening set and challenged Djokovic again in the second. After giving back a break of serve, Djokovic needed a medical timeout. He accepted a time violation while trying to regain his breath between points and consulted a trainer.

The 39-year-old then took control of the tie-break. In tennis, a tie-break decides a set when the players are level in games. In the deciding set, he won four consecutive games and finished with a backhand winner after two hours and 52 minutes. He has never lost in Beijing in 31 matches.

Djokovic was scheduled to face either Alexander Zverev or Shang Juncheng on Saturday for a quarter-final place.

Aryna Sabalenka had a smoother opening match, beating Mexico's Renata Zarazua 6-1 6-3 in 63 minutes. She struck 11 aces and faced no break points. In tennis, aces are serves that land legally without the receiver touching the ball. A break point gives the receiver a chance to win the server's game.

The world number two was playing her first match since losing both the top ranking and her US Open crown to Elena Rybakina in September. Her latest titles came in March, when she won Indian Wells and Miami back-to-back, a pairing known as the Sunshine Double.

Sabalenka explained that demanding more from herself sometimes drives her forward but sometimes drains her energy. She said she was working hard to be easier on herself. Her next opponent is Czech player Nikola Bartunkova, who nearly beat her at the Berlin Open in June.
why_it_matters: The article explains how Djokovic recovered after losing a set and how Sabalenka began her tournament successfully. Her comments also offer a player's view of the pressure created by demanding more from herself.
